items.title: JWST launch and arrival
items.claim: The James Webb Space Telescope launched on 25 December 2021. About how long to reach its operating point at L2?

options.text: About 30 days for L2 insertion; first science images released July 2022

items.reveal_title: About a month to L2; six months of commissioning before first science
items.reveal:
JWST inserted into L2 orbit on 24 January 2022. The first science images were released 12 July 2022.

The Sun-Earth L2 point lies about 1.5 million km from Earth.
items.why: Headline 'launch day' obscures months of staging required to make a telescope work.

items.title: Why we infer dark matter
items.claim: Vera Rubin and Kent Ford in the 1970s measured spiral galaxy rotation curves. What did they find?

options.text: Rotation slowed at the edges as Keplerian dynamics would predict
Rotation stayed roughly flat at large radii, implying more mass than visible matter accounted for

items.reveal_title: Flat rotation curves implied invisible mass
items.reveal:
Rubin and Ford's 1970s observations confirmed earlier hints (Zwicky 1933 on cluster dynamics).

Current cosmological models attribute roughly 27% of the universe's mass-energy budget to dark matter, 68% to dark energy and around 5% to baryonic matter.
items.why: Most of what controls galactic dynamics is something we cannot see directly.

items.title: How long photons take to escape the Sun
items.claim: A photon generated in the Sun's core takes how long, on average, to reach the surface?
items.reveal_title: Tens of thousands of years through a dense plasma
items.reveal:
The radiative zone is so opaque that photons random-walk outward. Mitalas and Sills (1992) modelled the escape time at about 10,000 to 170,000 years depending on assumptions.

Once free, the photon reaches Earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
items.why: The dramatic part of a photon's journey is hidden inside its source, not its trip across space.
